title: Unit 3 : Session 5 : SLO 1 — Booth's Multiplication Algorithm (Setup)
sections: 1. Fill in the Blanks (Remembering)
The single bit register Q-1 is initially set to 0.
The accumulator (A) and Q-1 are initialized to 0.
The sequence counter (SC) is set to the number of BITS in the multiplier.
The algorithm examines the last two bits of the Q and Q-1 registers to determine the next action.
2. True or False (Understanding)
a. If Q0 Q-1 = '10', perform A = A - M → TRUE
b. An arithmetic right shift is performed on A, Q and Q-1 in every cycle → TRUE
c. The algorithm stops when the sequence counter becomes 1 → FALSE (it stops when SC becomes 0)
d. If Q0 Q-1 = '01', perform A = A + M → TRUE
e. Booth's algorithm is only effective for multiplying positive numbers → FALSE
3. Matching (Applying)
a. 0 0 → 3. No operation
d. 1 1 → 3. No operation
4. Step-by-Step Analysis (Analyzing): (+7) × (-3), M = 0111, Q = 1101, A = 0000, Q-1 = 0
Step 1b: after arithmetic right shift → A = 1100, Q = 1110, Q-1 = 1.
Step 2c: new Q0 Q-1 = '01' → perform A = A + M: A = 1100 + 0111 = 0011.
Step 2d: after the second arithmetic right shift → A = 0001, Q = 1111, Q-1 = 0.
5. Algorithm Explanation (Creating)

Booth's algorithm multiplies signed 2's-complement numbers efficiently by handling blocks of 1s in the multiplier. Instead of adding for every 1, it performs one subtraction at the start of a run of 1s (pattern 10) and one addition at the end (pattern 01).

This reduces the number of arithmetic operations for long strings of 1s, and because it works directly on 2's-complement values it handles negative numbers with no extra sign logic, making multiplication faster and simpler in hardware.
